statement: Let d ≥ 2 and let u ≥ 0 be a local minimizer of the one-phase energy with volume coefficient 1 in an open set D ⊂ Rd. (i) There is a locally Lipschitz representative of u, and it is harmonic in {u > 0}. (ii) If x0 ∈ D ∩ ∂{u > 0}, every sequence rj ↓ 0 has a subsequence for which ux0,rj (y) := u(x0 + rjy) rj −→ U(y) (2.1) locally uniformly in Rd. The limit is a nonzero, nonnegative, one-homogeneous global minimizer. Along a further subsequence the convergence is strong in H1 loc, and the positivity indicators converge in L1 loc. (iii) If one such limit equals (y · e)+ with |e| = 1, then near x0 the free boundary is a smooth hypersurface and {u > 0} is exactly one of its sides. The function u is smooth up to that hypersurface from the positive side, and u = 0, ∇u = NE on the free boundary, (2.2) where NE is the Euclidean unit normal pointing into {u > 0}.
